title: Deskpin 1.5.1 - Find and sort files, and connection errors that say what went wrong

description.content: Filter box on both file panes. Type to narrow the folder you are looking at; it matches anywhere in the name, ignores case, and clears itself when you move to another folder. Refreshing, renaming or deleting keeps what you typed.

Sortable columns. Click NAME, SIZE or MODIFIED to sort, click the same header again to reverse it, and an arrow marks the column in use. Folders and files rank together - every row is ordered by the column you clicked, nothing is hoisted to the top.
A "No matches" state with a Clear filter button, so an empty pane tells you whether the folder is really empty or your filter is just too narrow.

Failing to open a machine now opens a dialog that names the failure and offers the fix: "Edit machine" when the sign-in details are missing or were rejected, "Try again" when the host could not be reached. The pane keeps the reason after you close it.

Connection problems are reported accurately. A machine that is switched off or has no SSH service was previously filed as an unexpected error, and the useful explanation of a rejected sign-in was replaced by a generic access-denied message.

Selecting a machine whose sign-in fails no longer stalls the app. A wrong password is an ordinary outcome of picking a machine, so connecting now returns it as a result instead of raising an exception.
SSH.NET updated to 2026.0.0. This closes the Terrapin vulnerability (CVE-2023-48795) present in the 2023.0.1 build shipped until now.
A rejected sign-in now records the server's own words in the log, which tells a wrong password apart from a server that refuses password authentication altogether.
The revealed password is now cleared when you switch machines while a connection is still being set up.
